_source: Terrain cards (15). keywords per rulebook p.66 + Keyword List.

iconLegend.[Move+Attack action]: wide black box with figure, plus sign and sword

terrain.name: Ruined Wall
terrain.text:
Destructible. Obscuring. Obstacle.
When this tile is destroyed, it turns into a Rubble Terrain tile.

terrain.name: Rubble
terrain.text:
Difficult Terrain.
When a Knight is involuntarily moved onto this tile, they suffer Knockdown.

terrain.name: Paleburrow
terrain.text:
Chasm. Obscuring.
When you are adjacent to this tile you may discard 1 Blood [Blood] token to lure out a Paleblood Worm that is not currently on the Board. If you do, place it on this tile.

terrain.name: Rut
terrain.text:
Indestructible.
If at any point of your Attack you are on this tile, your active Weapon gains Cumbersome for that Attack.
When a Monster moves onto this tile, flip it.

terrain.name: Swamp
terrain.text:
Difficult Terrain.
If you end your movement on this tile (voluntary or not), you die.
When you move through this tile, roll a [d10], adding +1 to the result for every Armor die on your Armor [Gear] cards. If the result is higher than your current [Vigor], you die.
When a Squire moves through or ends their movement on this tile, they die.

terrain.name: Primal Remnant
terrain.text:
Indestructible. Obstacle.
This tile always maintains adjacency to the Dragon. When the Dragon finishes its movement, move this tile along the shortest path to maintain a relative position. If you can't, immediately Remnant Move 4.
When this tile moves through or ends its movement on a Knight, that Knight dies.
When this tile moves through an Armor [Armor token] token, place it on the Primal Remnant Trait card.

terrain.name: Campfire
terrain.text:
Indestructible.
If you're adjacent to this tile, as a free action, you may gain +X [Heat] to place X Fire [Fire] tokens in the Knight Pool.
When a Knight moves through, ends their movement, or starts their turn on this tile and doesn't move until the end of turn, they lose -1 [Vigor] for every Metal [Gear] card they have and discard all their Flammable [Gear] cards.

terrain.name: Loose String
terrain.text:
Destructible.
When you end your movement on this tile, immediately place your miniature on the VP and remove this tile.

terrain.name: Bloodgeyser
terrain.text:
When a Paleblood Worm starts or ends its movement on this tile, place 1 Blood [Blood] token on its BP.
When a Knight starts or ends their movement on this tile, they discard the amount of Blood [Blood] tokens equal to their [Passion].

terrain.name: Slimy Throne
terrain.text:
Indestructible.
Treat this tile as a Blindspot.
If you are on this tile, as a free action, you may test Tenacity [Tenacity] (4+) to command the Throne to jump.
Success: The Throne listens to your command! Place this tile and your miniature on a chosen empty space without a Terrain tile.
Fail: Gain the Slimed Condition card.

terrain.name: Rotten Stump
terrain.text:
Obstacle. Destructible.
Search: If you're adjacent to a Rotten Stump Terrain tile, as a free action, you may roll a [d10]. You may gain +X [Heat] to add +X to your result:
1-2: Gain the Slimed Condition card.
3-4: You may place your Knight on an empty space adjacent to another Rotten Stump tile. Gain the Slimed Condition card.
5-10: You may place your Knight on an empty space adjacent to another Rotten Stump tile. If the Bog Witch is not on the Clash Board, you may place the Bog Witch on this Rotten Stump tile instead.
Each Rotten Stump may be Searched once per Round.

terrain.name: Tower
terrain.text:
Destructible. Obscuring. Obstacle.
When this tile is destroyed, it turns into a Rubble Terrain tile.
When you are about to be involuntarily moved from this tile, suffer Crash and ignore all Obstacles during this movement.
[Move+Attack action] Lunging Attack: If you're on a Tower, move up to your Speed [Speed] in a straight line until adjacent to a Monster and attack it. If your Attack hits, immediately move to the VP. Otherwise, suffer Knockdown.
unclear: Icon before 'Lunging Attack' is a wide black box with two glyphs and a plus sign (read as Move+Attack action, matching the gear-card convention).
